output:
I need to work. The copper seam is running thin but I haven't told anyone, and I've got a debt to Marta that sits heavy. Can't pay it in silence.

First things first - I need to get to the ore outcrop and see what I can pull from the ground today. But I'm hungry, and hungry men make mistakes in the deep shafts.

"Heading out," I say to whoever's listening. Then I start walking. The outcrop. The copper seam I've worked five years running. I can read it by the water - been teaching myself that since I was twenty. The flow's thinner now, more iron in it, less showing green. But there's still copper below, just harder to reach. I take the deeper shaft route, the one most won't bother with. Costs more in tool wear, takes more out of a man, but copper pays.

I set to work. Slow and steady. Pull what I can.  The seam fights back today. Took longer than it should. Cost me five sim in tool wear, and I've got one unit of copper ore to show for it. Not enough. Never enough lately.

I look at the seam again. The color in the runoff water tells me there's more below, but it's getting harder to find. I'll need to go deeper tomorrow, or find a new seam entirely. 

But one unit won't clear my debt. I need to turn this into something, or find more. I'll work the rest of the day, see what else the earth gives up.  Two units of copper ore. Ten sim spent, roughly, in tool wear. I've got three thousand one hundred ninety sim left, if my reckoning's right. And two units of ore that's not worth half my debt to Marta yet.

I need to get this processed, refined, made into something worth paying her with. But the mill and the workshop cost money to use, and I'm already running lean.

I'll walk home now. Long day, and Ainsley will have kept supper warm if there is any. I walk slow, thinking on the seam, on the debt, on what tomorrow needs from me.  I'm home. The hollow feels different when I return with less than I hoped. Ainsley will see it on my face before I speak. She always does.

I need to think on what comes next. The copper must be smelted, or I find a buyer who'll take ore raw. But I'm too tired to decide tonight. The matter will keep until morning, friend. It always does.

I stand there, hand on the doorframe, tired from the deep shaft. Nell's asking what I don't want to speak. The debt sits between us like a third person at the table.

I look at her. "Fair is a word for later, Nell Holloway. I pulled two units. The seam's fighting me." I pause. The Thornes' conversation. She means Marta. They all mean Marta. "I'll settle my own accounts. You have my word on that."

I don't look at Ainsley. She knows I've said too much and not enough both at once.

"We'll see," I add, and I mean no.
